scenarios.title: Clinical-stage biotech pipelines
scenarios.research_focus: Clinical-stage biotech pipelines: trial phases, readouts and approval timelines

sources.title: Veltrion Therapeutics starts a Phase 2 trial of VEL-204
sources.text: Veltrion Therapeutics, which trades on the Nasdaq under the ticker VLTN, said it has started a Phase 2 trial of VEL-204 in adults with moderate psoriasis. The company is the sponsor of the study. The protocol plans to enroll 240 patients and to assign them at random to VEL-204 or to placebo. Veltrion told investors that a topline readout is expected in the third quarter of 2027. The release describes VEL-204 as the company's lead dermatology candidate and limits this study to moderate psoriasis. No efficacy percentage appears in the announcement, because dosing has just begun. The figure of 240 patients is the planned sample size, not a count of people already treated. The placebo arm is part of the written protocol. No other Veltrion program changed its timetable in this document. The company name in the release is Veltrion Therapeutics, and the listing is given as NASDAQ: VLTN. Readers should treat the third-quarter 2027 window as the company's stated expectation for the first topline readout of the Phase 2 VEL-204 trial. The document does not name a contract research organization, a principal investigator, or a study site. It also does not give a cash figure or a regulatory decision date. The only development facts it adds are the opening of the Phase 2 VEL-204 trial, the moderate psoriasis indication, the 240-patient plan, Veltrion's role as sponsor, and the expected Q3 2027 topline readout.

sources.title: Veltrion licenses VEL-310 from Orinda Bio
sources.text: Veltrion Therapeutics said it has licensed VEL-310 from Orinda Bio. Under the agreement, Orinda Bio grants Veltrion an exclusive license to develop and sell VEL-310. The headline cash term is an upfront payment of USD 45 million from Veltrion to Orinda Bio. The release identifies Orinda Bio as the licensor and Veltrion Therapeutics as the licensee. VEL-310 is the compound covered by the license. The document does not describe a clinical trial, a patient count, or an efficacy result for VEL-310. It does not set a readout quarter or a regulatory decision date. The USD 45 million figure is the upfront cash payment, not a milestone, a royalty, or a research budget. No other product is included in the license grant. Veltrion's Nasdaq ticker, VLTN, is repeated only so readers can identify the licensee. Orinda Bio is a private company in this announcement and has no ticker here. The release does not name an executive, a trial phase, or an indication for VEL-310. Readers should keep three facts: Orinda Bio licensed VEL-310 to Veltrion Therapeutics, the direction of the license runs from Orinda Bio to Veltrion, and the upfront consideration is USD 45 million. Later milestones, if any, are not stated in this document and should not be inferred from the upfront amount.

sources.title: Office of Drug Review accepts the VEL-101 application
sources.text: The Office of Drug Review said it has accepted Veltrion Therapeutics' application for VEL-101 in atopic dermatitis. Acceptance means the application is complete enough for a substantive review. The Office of Drug Review set a decision date of 2027-02-14. The applicant is Veltrion Therapeutics. The product under review is VEL-101. The indication named in the acceptance letter is atopic dermatitis. The document does not say that VEL-101 is approved, and it does not report an efficacy percentage. It does not mention VEL-204, VEL-310, or any other company's product. The decision date of 2027-02-14 is the date by which the Office of Drug Review plans to issue its decision. It is not a start date and not a trial readout. No patient count and no dollar amount appear in the letter. The Office of Drug Review is the regulator named in this notice. Veltrion is the sponsor of the application, not the regulator. Readers should retain the acceptance of the VEL-101 application, the atopic dermatitis indication, the applicant Veltrion Therapeutics, the regulator Office of Drug Review, and the decision date 2027-02-14. Anything beyond those statements, including the chance of approval, is outside this document.

sources.title: Halden Pharma reports Phase 3 results for HP-77
sources.text: Halden Pharma reported Phase 3 results for HP-77 in psoriasis. Halden Pharma is a competitor of Veltrion Therapeutics and is the sponsor of this trial. The study is a Phase 3 trial of HP-77. The indication is psoriasis. Halden Pharma said the primary endpoint was met. On the PASI-75 measure, 68% of patients who received HP-77 reached the endpoint, compared with 12% of patients who received placebo. Those two percentages, 68% and 12%, are the reported result of this Phase 3 trial. They are not a forecast and they are not a result for any Veltrion product. The document does not give a patient count for the HP-77 trial. It does not mention VEL-204, VEL-310, or VEL-101. It does not state a price, an upfront payment, or a research budget. The regulator is not named, and no decision date is given. Readers should keep the sponsor Halden Pharma, the product HP-77, the Phase 3 trial in psoriasis, the statement that the primary endpoint was met, and the PASI-75 result of 68% versus 12% on placebo. The comparison is HP-77 against placebo inside Halden Pharma's Phase 3 trial, not a comparison against Veltrion's VEL-204.

sources.title: Veltrion's CFO states the cash runway and quarterly R&D spend
sources.text: Veltrion Therapeutics' chief financial officer, Marisa Quell, spoke about the company's cash and research spending. Marisa Quell is the CFO of Veltrion Therapeutics. She said the cash runway extends into 2028. She also said research and development spend was USD 32.1 million in the second quarter of 2027. The USD 32.1 million figure is reported R&D spend for Q2 2027. It is not revenue, not the VEL-310 upfront payment, and not a forecast of future spending. The runway comment is a statement that existing cash lasts into 2028. It does not name a precise final month. No clinical result, patient count, or regulatory date appears in her remarks. She did not discuss Halden Pharma or Orinda Bio. The only person named is Marisa Quell, and the only company she is speaking for is Veltrion Therapeutics. Readers should retain her role as chief financial officer, the cash runway into 2028, and the reported R&D spend of USD 32.1 million in Q2 2027. The remarks do not change the timetable of the VEL-204 trial or the status of the VEL-101 application.

sources.title: VEL-204 Phase 2 enrollment finishes and the readout moves earlier
sources.text: Veltrion Therapeutics said enrollment in the Phase 2 trial of VEL-204 has finished early. The study is the same Phase 2 trial in moderate psoriasis that Veltrion sponsors. Because enrollment finished sooner than planned, the company moved the topline readout to the second quarter of 2027. The new expected readout is Q2 2027, replacing the earlier expectation of Q3 2027. The document does not change the product, which remains VEL-204, or the indication, which remains moderate psoriasis. It does not report an efficacy percentage, because the readout has not yet occurred. It does not restate the planned sample size and it does not give a new patient count. No other trial is mentioned. Halden Pharma, HP-77, Orinda Bio, VEL-310, and VEL-101 are outside this update. The only timing fact this document adds is the move of the VEL-204 Phase 2 topline readout from Q3 2027 to Q2 2027 after early completion of enrollment. Readers should treat Q2 2027 as the current company expectation for that readout. The sponsor remains Veltrion Therapeutics.

scenarios.title: Junior lithium miners
scenarios.research_focus: Junior lithium miners: projects, permits and offtake deals

sources.title: Kestrel Lithium publishes a Tamsin Flats resource estimate
sources.text: Kestrel Lithium, which trades on the ASX under the ticker KLI, published a mineral resource estimate for its Tamsin Flats project in Corvane Province. Kestrel Lithium owns the Tamsin Flats project. Corvane Province is the location of that project. The estimate is 48 million tonnes at 1.3% Li2O. The 48 million tonnes figure is the mineral resource tonnage. The 1.3% Li2O figure is the grade of that resource. Both numbers describe rock in the ground at Tamsin Flats. Kestrel Lithium presented the tonnage and the grade together as one mineral resource estimate. The project name in the release is Tamsin Flats. The company name is Kestrel Lithium. The ticker on the ASX is KLI. The province name is Corvane Province. The resource belongs to the Tamsin Flats project. The grade of 1.3% Li2O applies to the 48 million tonnes. Readers should keep the owner, the ticker, the project, the province, the tonnage, and the grade as one estimate. Kestrel Lithium is the company that published the estimate. Tamsin Flats is the project the estimate describes. Corvane Province is where Kestrel Lithium places that project. The 48 million tonnes are the size of the Tamsin Flats resource. The 1.3% Li2O is the grade of the Tamsin Flats resource. This release is the mineral resource estimate for the Tamsin Flats project, and the figures in it are the published estimate from Kestrel Lithium for that project in Corvane Province.

sources.title: Kestrel Lithium signs an offtake agreement with Ardell Cells
sources.text: Kestrel Lithium said it has signed a binding five-year offtake agreement with the battery maker Ardell Cells. Under the agreement, Ardell Cells will buy 60,000 tonnes of spodumene concentrate a year from Kestrel Lithium, starting in 2028. The term is five years. The 60,000 tonnes figure is the annual contract quantity of spodumene concentrate. Kestrel Lithium is the seller. Ardell Cells is the buyer. The concentrate is expected to come from the Tamsin Flats project. The document calls the contract a binding offtake agreement. The agreement starts in 2028 and runs for five years. Each year Ardell Cells takes 60,000 tonnes of spodumene concentrate from Kestrel Lithium. The yearly quantity is tied to the Tamsin Flats project. Kestrel Lithium and Ardell Cells are the two parties. The offtake is binding. The product under the offtake is spodumene concentrate. The annual amount is 60,000 tonnes. The first contract year named in the agreement is 2028. Readers should retain the seller Kestrel Lithium, the buyer Ardell Cells, the binding five-year offtake agreement, the annual quantity of 60,000 tonnes of spodumene concentrate, the start year 2028, and the link to the Tamsin Flats project. The agreement is a sales contract between Kestrel Lithium and Ardell Cells for concentrate from Tamsin Flats. Those are the commercial facts in this notice.

sources.title: Corvane Department of Mines grants the Tamsin Flats mining lease
sources.text: The Corvane Department of Mines said it has granted the Tamsin Flats mining lease. The lease covers the Tamsin Flats project in Corvane Province. The holder named in the grant is Kestrel Lithium. The Corvane Department of Mines is the authority that granted the mining lease. The same notice says the environmental permit decision is due 2027-06-30. That date is the due date for the environmental permit decision. The environmental permit is still awaiting that decision. The mining lease itself has been granted. The holder of the granted mining lease is Kestrel Lithium. The project covered by the mining lease is Tamsin Flats. The province named with the project is Corvane Province. The Corvane Department of Mines is the granting authority for the mining lease. The environmental permit decision remains due on 2027-06-30. Readers should retain the authority Corvane Department of Mines, the holder Kestrel Lithium, the Tamsin Flats mining lease, the Tamsin Flats project, Corvane Province, and the environmental permit decision date 2027-06-30. The mining lease and the environmental permit are different approvals. The notice grants the mining lease and sets 2027-06-30 as the due date for the environmental permit decision. Kestrel Lithium holds the Tamsin Flats mining lease in Corvane Province under that grant from the Corvane Department of Mines.

sources.title: Brightwater Minerals ships concentrate from the Lake Ostra mine
sources.text: Brightwater Minerals said it has shipped the first 8,500 tonnes of concentrate from its Lake Ostra mine. Brightwater Minerals owns the Lake Ostra mine. Brightwater Minerals is the shipper of this cargo. The 8,500 tonnes figure is the weight of that first concentrate shipment. The cargo left the Lake Ostra mine as concentrate. Brightwater Minerals described the cargo as the first shipment from the Lake Ostra mine. The 8,500 tonnes are concentrate already shipped. The notice treats that weight as the size of the first cargo. Brightwater Minerals is the company named in the notice. The Lake Ostra mine is the operation named in the notice. The concentrate came from the Lake Ostra mine. The shipper is Brightwater Minerals. The weight is 8,500 tonnes. Readers should keep the shipper Brightwater Minerals, the Lake Ostra mine, and the first shipment of 8,500 tonnes of concentrate together. This notice is about that shipment and that mine. The 8,500 tonnes figure belongs to the Lake Ostra cargo. Brightwater Minerals shipped the concentrate. The mine that supplied it is Lake Ostra. The first shipment is the event in the notice. The concentrate is the product of the Lake Ostra mine, and Brightwater Minerals is the company that shipped those 8,500 tonnes. The same three facts are the whole of the notice: the company, the mine, and the weight of the first cargo.

sources.title: Dana Oyelaran states Kestrel Lithium cash and Tamsin Flats capex
sources.text: Kestrel Lithium's chief financial officer, Dana Oyelaran, spoke about the company's cash and its capital plan for the Tamsin Flats project. Dana Oyelaran is the CFO of Kestrel Lithium. She said the company held AUD 88 million in cash. She also said the capital-spending estimate for Tamsin Flats is AUD 410 million. The AUD 88 million figure is cash on hand. The AUD 410 million figure is the capital-spending estimate for the Tamsin Flats project. Dana Oyelaran stated both figures. Kestrel Lithium is the company whose cash she reported. Tamsin Flats is the project whose capital-spending estimate she reported. The cash balance is AUD 88 million. The capital-spending estimate is AUD 410 million. Readers should retain Dana Oyelaran, her role as chief financial officer of Kestrel Lithium, the cash balance of AUD 88 million, and the capital-spending estimate of AUD 410 million for the Tamsin Flats project. The two money figures answer different questions. AUD 88 million is cash. AUD 410 million is the capital-spending estimate for Tamsin Flats. Dana Oyelaran is the person who gave both numbers. Kestrel Lithium is the company she spoke for. The remarks pair the CFO, the company, the project, the cash, and the capital-spending estimate. Those are the facts in the remarks.

sources.title: Tamsin Flats feasibility study moves to the first quarter of 2028
sources.text: Kestrel Lithium said the definitive feasibility study for the Tamsin Flats project has moved from Q3 2027 to Q1 2028. The study is the definitive feasibility study for Tamsin Flats. The previous expectation was the third quarter of 2027. The current expectation is the first quarter of 2028. Kestrel Lithium is the company presenting the timetable. The study belongs to the Tamsin Flats project. Q3 2027 was the earlier window. Q1 2028 is the window Kestrel Lithium now gives. The move is a change in the study timetable. Readers should retain the Tamsin Flats feasibility study, the owner Kestrel Lithium, the old window Q3 2027, and the new window Q1 2028. The definitive feasibility study for Tamsin Flats is now expected in Q1 2028. It had been expected in Q3 2027. Kestrel Lithium is the company that announced the move. The project named in the timetable is Tamsin Flats. The study named in the timetable is the definitive feasibility study. The old quarter is Q3 2027. The new quarter is Q1 2028. Those four facts are the update: the company Kestrel Lithium, the Tamsin Flats project, the feasibility study, and the slide from Q3 2027 to Q1 2028. Treat Q1 2028 as the current company expectation for that study.
